docs.title: Linux Notes
docs.text:
Personal notes and references for Embedded Linux development on Renesas RZ boards.

Section What is in it Guides How to do things: flash the bootloader, boot over TFTP/NFS, boot from SD/eMMC. Works on every board. BSP Manual How modules work inside: architecture, diagrams, driver internals. Boards Board facts: device tree, boot switches, flash addresses.

Boards covered: RZ/G2L SMARC EVK, RZ/G3S SMARC EVK, RZ/V2N EVK.

docs.title: Boot mode switches
docs.text:
SW_MODE[1..3] select the boot mode. SW_MODE[4] sets the minimum input current of the USB-C power adapter (ON in the Start-up Guide examples).

SW_MODE[1] SW_MODE[2] SW_MODE[3] Function ON ON OFF eSD boot (3.3 V start-up) OFF ON OFF SCIF download ON OFF OFF eMMC boot (1.8 V) OFF OFF OFF SPI boot (1.8 V)

Useful SW_CONFIG settings (on the module):

SW_CONFIG Signal ON OFF 6 RZ_BOOTCPUSEL Cold boot from Cortex-M33 Cold boot from Cortex-A55 3 SW_SD2_EN SD2 disabled SD2 enabled 2 SW_SD0_DEV_SEL SD0 connected to uSD0 SD0 connected to eMMC 1 RZ_DEBUGEN JTAG debug disabled JTAG debug enabled

docs.title: BSP Manual
docs.text:
How the BSP modules work inside: architecture, data flow, driver internals and mapping tables. One page per module.

Module Driver Notes from MTU3 PWM drivers/pwm/pwm-rz-mtu3.c RZ/G3S

docs.title: Page template
docs.text:
# <Module name>

Driver: `drivers/<subsystem>/<file>.c`
Checked on: RZ/G3S (BSP version, kernel version)

## Overview
What the hardware block does and how Linux exposes it (sysfs, /dev, framework).

## Architecture
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    user["User space"] --> fw["Framework (pwm, gpio, ...)"] --> drv["Driver"] --> hw["HW block"]
```

## Device tree
The node and properties the driver needs.

## Driver internals
Probe flow, key structs, lookup tables.

## Test from user space
Commands to check that it works.

docs.title: Diagrams
docs.text:
Diagrams are written as Mermaid code blocks and follow the light/dark theme automatically:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User space
    participant D as Driver
    participant H as HW
    U->>D: write duty_cycle
    D->>H: update TGRB
```

Use flowchart for blocks and data paths, sequenceDiagram for call flows and stateDiagram-v2 for state machines. For diagrams Mermaid cannot draw (pinmux, clock trees), export an SVG from draw.io or Excalidraw into docs/imgs/.

docs.title: MTU3 PWM
docs.text:
Driver: drivers/pwm/pwm-rz-mtu3.c

The channel map below was written for the RZ/G3S.

docs.title: Lookup chain
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["hwpwm<br/>(0..15, sysfs export)"] --> B["rz_mtu3_get_channel()"]
    B --> C["channel_data[j]<br/>(j = 0..10)"]
    C --> D["->mtu / ->mtu_comp_pwm"]
    D --> E["HW channel<br/>(MTU0..MTU7)"]
  • hwpwm (0..15): the PWM number seen by the user in sysfs (export).
  • j (0..10): the index into channel_data[] and channel_map[].
  • Do not confuse these two numbers.

docs.title: PWM mode 1
docs.text:
Each IO pin is an independent PWM.

hwpwm Pin HW channel channel_data[j] channel_map[j] 0 MTIOC0A MTU0 [0] {0, 2} 1 MTIOC0C MTU0 [0] {0, 2} 2 MTIOC1A MTU1 [1] {2, 1} 3 MTIOC2A MTU2 [2] {3, 1} 4 MTIOC3A MTU3 [3] {4, 2} 5 MTIOC3C MTU3 [3] {4, 2} 6 MTIOC4A MTU4 [4] {6, 2} 7 MTIOC4C MTU4 [4] {6, 2} 8 MTIOC6A MTU6 [5] {8, 2} 9 MTIOC6C MTU6 [5] {8, 2} 10 MTIOC7A MTU7 [6] {10, 2} 11 MTIOC7C MTU7 [6] {10, 2}

Register selection rule in mode 1:

  • base == hwpwm: pin A, uses TIORH, TGRA (period), TGRB (duty).
  • base != hwpwm: pin C, uses TIORL, TGRC (period), TGRD (duty).

docs.title: Complementary PWM
docs.text:
Each PWM is a bundle of two pin pairs and uses two HW channels.

hwpwm Type Pair 1 (MTU3/MTU6) Pair 2 (MTU4/MTU7) HW channels channel_data[j] channel_map[j] 12 BD_AC MTIOC3B + 3D MTIOC4A + 4C MTU3 + MTU4 [7] {12, 1} 13 BD_BD MTIOC3B + 3D MTIOC4B + 4D MTU3 + MTU4 [8] {13, 1} 14 BD_AC MTIOC6B + 6D MTIOC7A + 7C MTU6 + MTU7 [9] {14, 1} 15 BD_BD MTIOC6B + 6D MTIOC7B + 7D MTU6 + MTU7 [10] {15, 1}

Notes:

  • channel_data[7] and [8] both point to MTU3 + MTU4. [9] and [10] both point to MTU6 + MTU7. They share the same hardware and differ only in which pins are enabled through TOER.
  • The enum name reads as "pair of MTU3/6" _ "pair of MTU4/7".

docs.title: channel_map[]
docs.text:
static const struct rz_mtu3_channel_io_map channel_map[] = {
	{ 0, 2 }, { 2, 1 }, { 3, 1 }, { 4, 2 }, { 6, 2 }, { 8, 2 }, { 10, 2 },
	{ 12, 1 }, { 13, 1 }, { 14, 1 }, { 15, 1 }
};
  • j = 0..6: mode 1.
  • j = 7..10: complementary.
  • Lookup rule: channel_data[j] serves hwpwm in the range [base, base + num_ios).

docs.title: Guides
docs.text:
Step-by-step procedures. Each guide works on every board; where a step differs, the page has a tab per board. Choosing a board in one tab switches the tabs on every page.

Guide When to use it Flashing the bootloader New board, or after rebuilding TF-A / U-Boot Booting with TFTP and NFS Daily development: kernel and rootfs stay on the host Booting from SD card and eMMC Standalone boot without the host

Typical order on a new board: flash the bootloader, boot over TFTP/NFS, then (optionally) write the images to SD or eMMC.

docs.title: Flashing the bootloader
docs.text:
The bootloader (BL2 + FIP with TF-A and U-Boot) lives in the SPI flash of the board. To write it, the board is put into SCIF download mode, a small program called the Flash Writer is sent to RAM over the serial console, and the Flash Writer then writes the BL2 and FIP files into flash with the XLS2 command.

The procedure is the same on every board. Only the file names, the flash addresses and the boot mode switches change. Pick your board in the tabs below; the choice is remembered on every page.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
All files come from the Yocto deploy directory (build/tmp/deploy/images/<machine>/).

RZ/G2LRZ/G3SRZ/V2N

There are 2 versions of the RZ/G2L SMARC EVK: PMIC and non-PMIC.

File non-PMIC PMIC Flash Writer Flash_Writer_SCIF_RZG2L_SMARC_DDR4_2GB.mot Flash_Writer_SCIF_RZG2L_SMARC_PMIC_DDR4_2GB_1PCS.mot BL2 bl2_bp-smarc-rzg2l.srec bl2_bp-smarc-rzg2l_pmic.srec FIP fip-smarc-rzg2l.srec fip-smarc-rzg2l_pmic.srec File Name Flash Writer FlashWriter-smarc-rzg3s.mot BL2 bl2_bp_spi-smarc-rzg3s.srec FIP fip-smarc-rzg3s.srec File Name Flash Writer Flash_Writer_SCIF_RZV2N_DEV_LPDDR4X.mot BL2 bl2_bp_spi-rzv2n-evk.srec FIP fip-rzv2n-evk.srec

docs.title: Flash addresses
docs.text:
Values to type at the XLS2 prompts (hex, without the H' prefix):

Board BL2 Program Top BL2 Save Address FIP Program Top FIP Save Address RZ/G2L 11E00 00000 00000 1D200 RZ/G3S A1E00 00000 00000 60000 RZ/V2N 8101E00 00000 00000 60000

Note

These addresses depend on the BSP version. If writing succeeds but the board does not boot, check the Start-up Guide that matches your BSP (see Boards).

docs.title: Serial console
docs.text:
Connect the debug serial port of the board to the host and open a terminal (Tera Term, minicom, picocom, ...) with 115200 bps, 8N1, no flow control.

picocom -b 115200 /dev/ttyUSB0

docs.title: Boot mode: SCIF download
docs.text:
Power off the board and set the boot mode switches to SCIF download:

RZ/G2LRZ/G3SRZ/V2N

Configure SW11 as below:

Set SW_MODE (carrier board) as below:

SW_MODE 1 2 3 4 Setting OFF ON OFF ON

Set DSW1 to Boot mode 3 (SCIF download). See the figure in the RZ/V AI SDK guide for the switch positions.

Power on (or press RESET). The terminal shows:

SCIF Download mode
(C) Renesas Electronics Corp.
-- Load Program to SystemRAM ---------------
please send !

docs.title: Flashing
docs.text:
1. Flash Writer

Send the Flash Writer .mot file from the terminal (Tera Term: File → Send file). When it is loaded, the > prompt appears.

2. BL2

>XLS2
===== Qspi writing of RZ/G2 Board Command =============
Load Program to Spiflash
Writes to any of SPI address.
Micron : MT25QU512
Program Top Address & Qspi Save Address
===== Please Input Program Top Address ============
 Please Input : H'11E00
===== Please Input Qspi Save Address ===
 Please Input : H'00000
Work RAM(H'50000000-H'53FFFFFF) Clear....
please send ! ('.' & CR stop load)

Enter the BL2 addresses of your board from the table above, then send the BL2 .srec file. If the Flash Writer asks SPI Data Clear(H'FF) Check ... Clear OK?(y/n), answer y.

3. FIP

>XLS2
===== Qspi writing of RZ/G2 Board Command =============
Load Program to Spiflash
Writes to any of SPI address.
Micron : MT25QU512
Program Top Address & Qspi Save Address
===== Please Input Program Top Address ============
 Please Input : H'00000
===== Please Input Qspi Save Address ===
 Please Input : H'1D200
Work RAM(H'50000000-H'53FFFFFF) Clear....
please send ! ('.' & CR stop load)

Enter the FIP addresses of your board, then send the FIP .srec file.

The logs above are from the RZ/G2L. The messages differ slightly on other boards, but the prompts are the same.

RZ/G2LRZ/G3SRZ/V2N

Tip

The RZ/G3S Flash Writer supports a SUP command to raise the transfer rate from 115200 to 921600 bps before XLS2. Change the terminal speed to match, and change it back to 115200 bps when writing is done.

No board-specific notes.

Set SW11 to normal boot:

Set SW_MODE to SPI boot:

SW_MODE 1 2 3 4 Setting OFF OFF OFF ON

Set DSW1 to Boot mode 2 (xSPI boot).

You should see U-Boot start, for example on the RZ/G2L:

docs.title: Booting with TFTP and NFS
docs.text:
During development, the fastest loop is to keep everything on the host: U-Boot loads the kernel Image and the device tree over TFTP, and the kernel mounts its root filesystem over NFS. A rebuilt kernel or a changed file in the rootfs is picked up on the next boot without touching the board's storage.

Host (Ubuntu)                          Board
/srv/tftp/Image, <board>.dtb  --TFTP-->  U-Boot (RAM)
/nfs/<board>/  (rootfs)       --NFS--->  Linux root=/dev/nfs

The host setup is the same for every board. Only the device tree name (and, if they differ, the load addresses) change in the U-Boot config.

docs.title: Set up the TFTP server
docs.text:
Install tftp-hpa (/srv/tftp/ is used as the TFTP directory):

sudo apt-get install tftpd-hpa

Check the status of tftpd-hpa:

service tftpd-hpa status

Disable the firewall:

sudo ufw disable

docs.title: Set up the NFS server
docs.text:
Install the NFS server:

sudo apt-get install nfs-kernel-server

Start the NFS server:

sudo /etc/init.d/nfs-kernel-server start

Check the status of the NFS service:

service nfs-kernel-server status

Create one directory per board, for example /nfs/rzg2l:

sudo mkdir -p /nfs/rzg2l

Open /etc/exports:

sudo vim /etc/exports

Add one line per board directory:

/nfs/rzg2l *(rw,no_subtree_check,sync,no_root_squash)

Make the NFS server read /etc/exports again:

sudo exportfs -a

Confirm the export is active:

showmount -e localhost

docs.title: Prepare Image, DTB and rootfs
docs.text:
Copy Image and the device tree of your board to /srv/tftp/:

sudo cp <Image path> <device tree path> /srv/tftp/
Board Device tree RZ/G2L r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb RZ/G3S r9a08g045s33-smarc.dtb RZ/V2N r9a09g056n48-rzv2n-evk.dtb

Extract the rootfs (*.tar.bz2) into the board directory:

sudo tar -xf <rootfs>.tar.bz2 -C /nfs/rzg2l

docs.title: Set a static IP on the host
docs.text:
If the host is a virtual machine, attach a network adapter in bridged mode to the Ethernet port connected to the board.

Select Devices → Network → Network Settings:

Configure the adapter as below:

Find the interface connected to the board with ifconfig (or ip addr):

rvc@linux:~$ ifconfig
enp0s3: flags=4163<UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,MULTICAST>  mtu 1500
        inet 10.0.2.15  netmask 255.255.255.0  broadcast 10.0.2.255
        ...

enx080027effb07: flags=4163<UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,MULTICAST>  mtu 1500
        inet 192.168.1.3  netmask 255.255.255.0  broadcast 192.168.1.255
        ether 08:00:27:ef:fb:07  txqueuelen 1000  (Ethernet)
        ...

In this example the board is on enx080027effb07. To make the static IP permanent, add to /etc/network/interfaces:

auto lo
iface lo inet loopback

iface enx080027effb07 inet static
address 192.168.1.3   # <IP>
netmask 255.255.255.0 # <netmask>

Then reboot. To set it only for the current session:

sudo ifconfig enx080027effb07 192.168.1.3

The rest of this page uses 192.168.1.3 for the host and 192.168.1.5 for the board.

docs.text:
Connect the serial console and an Ethernet port of the board to the host.

docs.title: U-Boot config on the board
docs.text:
Power on the board and press any key to stop autoboot.

Set a MAC address (only needed if U-Boot reports address not set):

setenv ethaddr 74:90:50:00:00:d6

Set the board IP and the server IP:

setenv ipaddr 192.168.1.5
setenv serverip 192.168.1.3

Set bootcmd to load the kernel and the device tree over TFTP, and bootargs to mount the rootfs over NFS:

RZ/G2LRZ/G3SRZ/V2N 
setenv bootcmd 'tftp 0x48080000 Image; tftp 0x48000000 r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb; booti 0x48080000 - 0x48000000'
setenv bootargs 'console=ttySC0,115200n8 ip=192.168.1.5:192.168.1.3::::eth0 rootwait root=/dev/nfs rw nfsroot=192.168.1.3:/nfs/rzg2l,nfsvers=3,tcp noinitrd nohlt panic=1 earlyprintk=ttySC0,115200n8'

setenv bootcmd 'tftp 0x48080000 Image; tftp 0x48000000 r9a08g045s33-smarc.dtb; booti 0x48080000 - 0x48000000'
setenv bootargs 'console=ttySC0,115200n8 ip=192.168.1.5:192.168.1.3::::eth0 rootwait root=/dev/nfs rw nfsroot=192.168.1.3:/nfs/rzg3s,nfsvers=3,tcp'

The load addresses match the default boot of the RZ/G3S Start-up Guide. The bootargs have not been tested on this board yet.

Not tested yet. Read the default environment first and reuse its load addresses and console:

printenv bootcmd bootargs

Device tree: r9a09g056n48-rzv2n-evk.dtb.

What the parameters mean:

  • tftp <addr> <file>: load a file from serverip into RAM.
  • booti <kernel> - <fdt>: boot an arm64 Image. The - means there is no initramfs.
  • ip=<board>:<server>::::eth0: configure the network in the kernel before mounting the rootfs.
  • root=/dev/nfs nfsroot=<server>:<dir>: mount the rootfs over NFS.

Tip

On a new board, printenv shows the default bootcmd and bootargs. Reuse its load addresses and console= value, and change only the TFTP and NFS parts.

Save the environment if you want the board to always boot this way (optional):

saveenv

Check the connection:

ping 192.168.1.3

Boot:

boot

Expected log (RZ/G2L):

Hit any key to stop autoboot:  0
Using ethernet@11c20000 device
TFTP from server 192.168.1.3; our IP address is 192.168.1.5
Filename 'Image'.
Load address: 0x48080000

         ...
done

docs.title: Booting from SD card and eMMC
docs.text:
Instead of loading the kernel over the network every time, Image, the device tree and the root filesystem can be stored on a micro SD card or on the on-module eMMC. U-Boot (in SPI flash, see Flashing the bootloader) then loads them with ext4load.

Both media use the same layout:

Partition Size Filesystem Content 1 1 GB ext4 Image, <board>.dtb 2 remaining ext4 Root filesystem

The procedure is the same on every board. What changes is the device tree name and how Linux and U-Boot number the MMC devices:

RZ/G2LRZ/G3SRZ/V2N Medium Linux device U-Boot device eMMC (on SoM) /dev/mmcblk0 mmc 0 micro SD (carrier board) /dev/mmcblk1 mmc 1

Device tree: r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb

U-Boot lists 3 SD hosts: sd@11c00000: 0, sd@11c10000: 1, sd@11c20000: 2.

  • SD0 (mmc 0) is connected either to the eMMC or to the micro SD slot uSD0, selected by SW_CONFIG[2] on the module (OFF = eMMC, ON = uSD0).
  • With the default settings, the Start-up Guide boots Linux from the micro SD card on mmc 1.

Check the Linux device names with lsblk before partitioning.

Device tree: r9a08g045s33-smarc.dtb

Medium Linux device U-Boot device eMMC /dev/mmcblk0 not checked

Check the micro SD device name with lsblk.

Device tree: r9a09g056n48-rzv2n-evk.dtb

Note

The steps below are run on the board, after booting Linux with TFTP and NFS. This is the only way to write to the eMMC. Copy Image, the device tree and the rootfs tarball into the NFS rootfs (for example to /nfs/<board>/home/root/) so they are available on the board.

An SD card can also be prepared on a Linux host with a card reader. In that case the card shows up as /dev/sdX (check with lsblk) instead of /dev/mmcblkN.

The commands below use the RZ/G2L SD card (/dev/mmcblk1). Replace the device with the one of your board and medium.

docs.title: Create partitions
docs.text:
Danger

Partitioning erases all data on the device. Double-check the device name with lsblk before continuing.

Unmount any partitions that were mounted automatically, then open fdisk:

umount /dev/mmcblk1p* 2>/dev/null
fdisk /dev/mmcblk1

Create partition 1 (1 GB) for the kernel and device tree:

Command (m for help): o                                # new empty DOS partition table
Command (m for help): n
Partition type
   p   primary (0 primary, 0 extended, 4 free)
   e   extended (container for logical partitions)
Select (default p): <Enter>
Partition number (1-4, default 1): <Enter>
First sector (2048-62333951, default 2048): <Enter>
Last sector, +/-sectors or +/-size{K,M,G,T,P} (...): +1G

Create partition 2 using the remaining space for the root filesystem:

Command (m for help): n
Select (default p): <Enter>
Partition number (2-4, default 2): <Enter>
First sector (...): <Enter>
Last sector, +/-sectors or +/-size{K,M,G,T,P} (...): <Enter>

Write the partition table and exit:

Command (m for help): w

docs.title: Format partitions
docs.text:
mkfs.ext4 -L boot   /dev/mmcblk1p1
mkfs.ext4 -L rootfs /dev/mmcblk1p2

docs.title: Copy kernel, device tree and rootfs
docs.text:
Copy Image and the device tree to partition 1:

mount /dev/mmcblk1p1 /mnt
cp ~/Image ~/<board>.dtb /mnt/
sync
umount /mnt

Extract the root filesystem to partition 2:

mount /dev/mmcblk1p2 /mnt
tar -xf ~/<rootfs>.tar.bz2 -C /mnt
sync
umount /mnt

Tip

Extract the tarball directly into the mount point with tar -C rather than copying the archive onto the partition first. This avoids leaving a large .tar.bz2 file in the root filesystem.

docs.title: U-Boot config
docs.text:
Power on the board and press any key to stop autoboot.

The general form is:

setenv bootcmd 'mmc dev <N>; ext4load mmc <N>:1 <kernel addr> Image; ext4load mmc <N>:1 <fdt addr> <board>.dtb; booti <kernel addr> - <fdt addr>'
setenv bootargs 'console=<console> rootwait root=/dev/mmcblk<M>p2 rw'
  • <N>: U-Boot MMC device number, <M>: Linux MMC device number (see the table at the top).
  • <kernel addr> / <fdt addr>: the same load addresses as in the TFTP setup.
RZ/G2LRZ/G3SRZ/V2N

SD card:

setenv bootcmd 'mmc dev 1; ext4load mmc 1:1 0x48080000 Image; ext4load mmc 1:1 0x48000000 r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb; booti 0x48080000 - 0x48000000'
setenv bootargs 'console=ttySC0,115200n8 rootwait root=/dev/mmcblk1p2 rw noinitrd nohlt panic=1 earlyprintk=ttySC0,115200n8'

eMMC:

setenv bootcmd 'mmc dev 0; ext4load mmc 0:1 0x48080000 Image; ext4load mmc 0:1 0x48000000 r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb; booti 0x48080000 - 0x48000000'
setenv bootargs 'console=ttySC0,115200n8 rootwait root=/dev/mmcblk0p2 rw noinitrd nohlt panic=1 earlyprintk=ttySC0,115200n8'

Not tested yet. Fill in the general form with r9a08g045s33-smarc.dtb, the MMC numbers above and the load addresses 0x48080000 (kernel) / 0x48000000 (fdt).

Not tested yet. Run printenv bootcmd bootargs to see the default load addresses and console, then fill in the general form.

What the commands do:

  • mmc dev <N>: select the MMC device.
  • ext4load mmc <dev>:<part> <addr> <file>: load a file from an ext4 partition into RAM.
  • booti <kernel> - <fdt>: boot an arm64 Image. The - means there is no initramfs.
  • root=/dev/mmcblkXp2 rootwait: mount partition 2 as rootfs, and wait until the MMC device is ready.

Warning

The file names in ext4load must match the files on partition 1 exactly. If you stored them under other names (for example Image_scif), update bootcmd accordingly.

Before saving, you can check that U-Boot sees the files:

mmc dev 1
ext4ls mmc 1:1

Save the environment so the board boots this way automatically (optional), then boot:

saveenv
boot

docs.title: Network access after boot (optional)
docs.text:
Unlike NFS boot, the kernel does not configure Ethernet when booting from SD/eMMC. To reach the board from the host (for ssh, scp, ...), bring up eth0 with a static IP on the same subnet as the host:

ip link set eth0 up
ip addr add 192.168.1.5/24 dev eth0
ip addr show eth0
ping 192.168.1.3      # host IP

The host can then connect with ssh root@192.168.1.5. This setting is lost on reboot.
